endow

en-DOW · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To endow is to gift a quality, ability, or asset.

Nature seemed to endow the youngest sister with an unusually quick wit, while her siblings had to work harder for every joke.

Example

The retired opera singer used her entire estate to endow a foundation that pays for free voice lessons for children who could never otherwise afford them.

Setting up a permanent, ongoing source of support, here a foundation that will keep funding lessons for years to come, is exactly what it means to endow something.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

bestow: To bestow is to present something as a gift or honor in a single formal act -- a medal, a title, a prize -- and the giving is complete the moment it changes hands. To endow reaches further in time: it sets up support that keeps flowing long after the original gift.

furnish: To furnish is to supply someone or something with what is needed right now -- desks for a classroom, proof for a court -- and the job ends once the need is met. To endow is to plant a source that keeps producing support year after year.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

deprive: take away something needed

strip: remove entirely, often forcefully

Where it sits · how grand and lasting the giving — provide → endow → lavish

provide vs. endow: Provide is weaker than endow: to provide supplies meets a need for now, while to endow goes further, granting a lasting gift or ability meant to endure.

lavish vs. endow: Lavish is stronger than endow: a donor may endow a scholarship with a generous gift, but to lavish money is to pour it out with even heavier, unrestrained abundance.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — dow-/dot- (dos, dotare)

root — dow-/dot- (dos, dotare): a dowry; to give a dowry (Latin, via Old French endouer)

Put it together

Put it together: Endow comes from Old French endouer, rooted in Latin dos, 'a dowry' -- the property a bride traditionally brought into a marriage. To endow something is to permanently furnish it with resources, the way a dowry once permanently provided for a new household.

Use the root in a new word: dowry

Use the root in a new word: dowry: In the old story, the merchant's daughter brought a dowry of gold coins and fine silk into her marriage.

Root Check

Word Choice

Endow describes an ongoing, structural kind of giving -- setting something up so it keeps producing support long after the original gift. Compare bequeath (later in this unit), which specifically means to leave something to someone through a will, after death.
